To truly understand traffic dynamics, we must first recognize that a road is not just a static strip of asphalt; it is a complex system influenced by a dynamic web of external and internal factors. High adhesion means the car can brake quickly and turn sharply without sliding; low adhesion (like on ice or wet pavement) drastically increases braking distance and limits safe speed. Furthermore, the **condition of the drivers** introduces a human element: a fatigued or inexperienced driver has slower reaction times, effectively increasing the distance needed to stop.
